newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: RUGBY-SPRINGBOKS AND PUMAS BOTH VICTORY THIRSTY.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY-SPRINGBOKS AND PUMAS BOTH VICTORY THIRSTY.

text.p: The South African Springboks and the Argentine Pumas both have something to prove when they meet on Saturday in the first of two rugby test matches in Buenos Aires.

The South Africans, the world champions, must be considered favourites, but they are at the end of a heavy season in which they have won just three of eight tests. Now they are starting a tour which takes them from Argentina to Wales and France.

Argentina is considered the easiest leg of the tour and good victories are essential to silence criticism at home about the poor quality of their recent play and the selection of the tour squad, specially the dropping of captain Francois Pienaar.

The Springboks certainly began their tour well last Tuesday against the Rosario selection which has proved the undoing of a number of touring sides lately. The Springboks won impressively by building up a big lead with five tries in 25 minutes and running out 45-36 winners.
This gave the impression that they could turn on the heat whenever needed, but they will also have to be careful against the fighting spirit of the Pumas and not let up pressure.

The Argentines meanwhile feel on top of the world after retaining the Pan American title in Canada in September when more than half their team was composed of newcomers. They also played 15-man attacking rugby, the style preferred by their coach, Jose Luis Imhoff.

For the first test they have brought back a number of experienced players, some of whom could not travel to Canada, and the lineup shows no real surprise apart from the absence of injured Diego Albanese and veteran Diego Cuesta Silva who preferred to go to a world senior championship (for over 35s) in Bermuda.

But it does include the first ever professional in a Pumas team -- hooker Federico Mendez, who played for Natal this year and has just signed a reported $120,000 contract with English club champions Bath for next season. With the Pumas, however, he will collect only the same expense allowance given to the rest of the team.

Argentine rugby is still amateur, but the ban on including foreign-based players in the national team has been lifted. Mendez will also play for his native province, Mendoza, when they face ths Springboks next week.

Springboks: 15-Andre Joubert 14-James Small 13-Japie Mulder 12-Hennie le Roux 11-Jacques Olivier 10-Henry Honiball 9-Joost van der Oosthuizen 8-Gary Teichmann (captain) 7-Andre Venter 6-Ruben Kruger 5-Mark Andrews 4-Kobus Wiese 3-Adrian Garvey 2-James Dalton 1-Dawie Theron.
Replacements: Andre Snyman, Kevin Putt, Fritz van Heerden, Wayne Fyvie, Toks van der Linde, Henry Tromp.

Pumas: 15-Roberto Grau, 14-Federico Mendez, 13-Omar Hasan Jalil, 12-German Llanes, 11-Pedro Sporleder, 10-Rolando Martin, 9-Raul Perez, 8-Pablo Camerlinckx, 7-Jose Luis Cilley, 6-Nicolas Fernandez Miranda, 5-Tomas Solari, 4-Lisandro Arbizu (captain), 3-Gonzalo Camardon, 2-Octavio Bartolucci, 1-Facundo Soler.
